key: Ask when the organism reaches the baby: transplacental infections injure the fetus during pregnancy and are prevented by protecting the mother beforehand, while birth-canal infections strike at delivery and are prevented by acting at delivery.
items: Toxoplasma crosses the placenta after a primary maternal infection, so the injury happens in utero and prevention means avoiding cat litter and raw meat.
Rubella reaches the embryo through maternal blood in the first trimester; only vaccination before pregnancy prevents it.
Cytomegalovirus crosses the placenta and injures the developing brain months before birth.
The virus crosses the placenta and destroys fetal red cell precursors, so hydrops develops during pregnancy.
Maternal chickenpox before 20 weeks seeds the fetus through the placenta while the limbs are forming.
Treponema pallidum crosses the placenta at any stage of pregnancy, so penicillin during pregnancy prevents it.
Zika virus infects fetal neural progenitor cells after crossing the placenta, so the brain injury is prenatal.
The newborn inhales or swallows colonizing streptococci during labor, which is why penicillin in labor prevents it.
Neonatal herpes after vaginal birth with lesions
Most neonatal herpes comes from contact with virus in the birth canal, so cesarean prevents it when lesions are present.
Gonococci enter the eye during passage through an infected cervix; eye ointment at birth prevents it.
Chlamydia is picked up in the birth canal, so screening and treating the mother before delivery prevents it.
Hepatitis B in an infant of an HBsAg-positive mother
Most transmission happens around delivery, so HBIG and vaccine within 12 hours of birth prevent it.
